title: A Phase 1b/2, Randomised, Placebo-controlled Study to Evaluate Safety, Tolerability, Efficacy, and Immunogenicity of VTP-200, a Chimpanzee Adenovirus and Modified Vaccinia Ankara-vectored Multigenotype High-risk Human Papillomavirus Vaccine in Women With Low-grade Cervical Lesions.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The clearance of high-risk oncogenic human papillomaviruses (hrHPV) and related cervical lesions is associated with the development of a robust T-cell response. Therapeutic vaccination that induces HPV antigen-specific T cells is a promising approach.
analysis.study_design_and_population: An open-label lead-in was followed by a randomized, blinded, placebo-controlled main phase. Nine participants were enrolled in the lead-in and 99 were randomized 67:32 to 5 active dose arms or placebo, respectively.
analysis.methods: A 2-vector dosing strategy using Chimpanzee Adenovirus Oxford 1-HPV and Modified Vaccinia virus Ankara-HPV, both encoding the same multiantigen HPV cassette was given on a 0/28-day schedule to participants with persistent cervical hrHPV and a history of low-grade cervical lesions.
analysis.main_results: The regimens were well-tolerated with no grade 3-related treatment emergent adverse events or serious adverse reactions. All dosing regimens generated antigen-specific CD4+ and CD8+ T-cell responses. There was no difference in hrHPV clearance between the pooled active groups and placebo (20/64 [31.3%] versus 10/30 [33.3%]; P > .99), nor in lesion clearance.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: A heterologous, multiantigenic HPV 2-component immunotherapy regimen was well-tolerated and immunogenic but did not result in a statistically significant clearance of either hrHPV or the associated cervical lesions in women with persistent high-risk HPV infections.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that while the vaccine is safe and induces immune responses, it does not significantly improve hrHPV clearance or lesion resolution in this population, indicating a need for further optimization of therapeutic HPV vaccines.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was limited by its sample size and the lack of statistically significant difference in hrHPV clearance, though the highest dose showed a trend toward higher clearance. The evidence strength is moderate due to the randomized design but limited by the small sample size and lack of long-term follow-up.

analysis.summary_en: This phase 1b/2 randomized, placebo-controlled study evaluated the safety, tolerability, efficacy, and immunogenicity of VTP-200, a chimpanzee adenovirus and modified vaccinia Ankara-vectored multigenotype high-risk human papillomavirus vaccine in women with low-grade cervical lesions. The study included an open-label lead-in with 9 participants and a main phase with 99 randomized participants (67 active, 32 placebo). The vaccine was well-tolerated with no serious adverse events and induced antigen-specific CD4+ and CD8+ T-cell responses. However, there was no statistically significant difference in hrHPV clearance (31.3% vs 33.3%; P > .99) or lesion clearance between active and placebo groups. The highest dose showed a trend toward higher hrHPV clearance (60%). The authors conclude that while the vaccine is immunogenic, it did not significantly improve hrHPV clearance or lesion resolution in this population.

title: The Association Between Human Papillomavirus and Prostate Cancer: A Systematic Review and Meta‐Analysis

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to synthesize epidemiological evidence on the association between human papillomavirus (HPV) and prostate cancer, addressing the controversy surrounding HPV's role in prostate carcinogenesis despite frequent detection in prostate specimens.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 84 articles (1990–2025), including 57 cross-sectional, 15 case-control, 6 nested case-control, and 6 cohort studies, was conducted to evaluate the relationship between HPV and prostate cancer.
analysis.methods: The researchers performed a systematic search of Embase, MEDLINE, Scopus, and Cochrane on January 31, 2025, with two independent reviewers screening articles and extracting data; pooled risk estimates were calculated using a random effects model, with subgroup analyses by HPV risk level, genotype, and control group.
analysis.main_results: The meta-analysis of 39 studies yielded a pooled odds ratio (OR) of 2.35 (95% CI: 1.87–2.95) for HPV and prostate cancer, with a higher OR of 2.75 (95% CI: 1.69–4.46) for high-risk HPV; HPV16, HPV18, and HPV33 showed positive associations, and the strongest association was observed when using normal tissue as controls (OR: 4.81, 95% CI: 1.83–12.69).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as supporting a positive association between oncogenic HPV DNA detection in prostate specimens and prostate cancer, though they noted that its etiologic significance remains unclear.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest a potential role for HPV in prostate carcinogenesis, which may inform surveillance strategies and further research into HPV's mechanisms in prostate cancer development.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is moderate, limited by the heterogeneity of study designs, HPV detection methods, and the inability to establish causality; most studies reported HPV prevalence below 20%, and the etiologic significance of HPV in prostate cancer remains uncertain.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review and meta-analysis synthesized epidemiological evidence on the association between human papillomavirus (HPV) and prostate cancer. The study included 84 articles (1990–2025) and found a pooled odds ratio of 2.35 (95% CI: 1.87–2.95) for HPV and prostate cancer, with a higher association for high-risk HPV (OR: 2.75, 95% CI: 1.69–4.46). HPV16, HPV18, and HPV33 showed positive associations, with the strongest effect when normal tissue was used as controls (OR: 4.81, 95% CI: 1.83–12.69). While the findings support a link between HPV detection and prostate cancer, the etiologic significance remains unclear, and the evidence is limited by study heterogeneity and low HPV prevalence in most samples.

title: Self-collected versus clinician-collected human papillomavirus samples.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the comparability of self-collected and clinician-collected samples for human papillomavirus detection, cytological findings, and identification of infectious agents.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This prospective controlled clinical trial enrolled 124 women aged 30-65 years who were eligible for routine cervical cancer screening. Participants were allocated to either a clinician-collected control group (n=51) or a self-collected group (n=73) via systematic allocation based on clinic registration order.
analysis.methods: Viral deoxyribonucleic acid analysis was performed by multiplex real-time polymerase chain reaction; cytological evaluation followed the Bethesda classification system. Infectious agents and participant satisfaction were also assessed. Laboratory personnel were blinded to group allocation.
analysis.main_results: Overall human papillomavirus positivity was 21.8% (27/124), with rates of 27.5% (14/51) in the control group and 17.8% (13/73) in the self-collected group (p=0.200). Cytological abnormalities were detected in 5.5% of self-collected samples versus 0% in the control group (p=0.236). Inflammatory smear findings, Candida (9.8 vs. 8.2%), and Trichomonas vaginalis (0 vs. 1.4%) detection rates were similar between groups. Mean satisfaction score was 12.6±1.62 out of 16 (78.8% positive responses).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Self-collected human papillomavirus sampling yields results diagnostically comparable to clinician-collected specimens. Self-collected human papillomavirus sampling demonstrated similar human papillomavirus detection rates compared with clinician-collected specimens.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Given its feasibility and high acceptability, self-collection may serve as an effective complementary approach in cervical cancer screening programs, particularly for reaching women who have not previously participated in screening.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report specific limitations of the study design or evidence strength assessment.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the comparability of self-collected and clinician-collected samples for human papillomavirus (HPV) detection, cytological findings, and identification of infectious agents in a prospective controlled clinical trial involving 124 women aged 30-65 years. HPV positivity rates were 27.5% in the clinician-collected group and 17.8% in the self-collected group, with no significant difference (p=0.200). Cytological abnormalities were detected in 5.5% of self-collected samples versus 0% in the clinician-collected group (p=0.236). Inflammatory smear findings, Candida, and Trichomonas vaginalis detection rates were similar between groups. The mean satisfaction score was 12.6±1.62 out of 16 (78.8% positive responses). The authors concluded that self-collected HPV sampling is diagnostically comparable to clinician-collected specimens and may serve as an effective complementary approach in cervical cancer screening programs, especially for women not previously participating in screening. The study does not report specific limitations or evidence strength assessment.

title: The cervicovaginal microbiome: an emerging determinant of HPV infection and disease

analysis.scope_and_question: This review focuses on human papillomaviruses (HPVs), specifically their role in causing diseases ranging from cutaneous warts to invasive cancers, with emphasis on high-risk HPVs that are oncogenic and associated with cervical, anogenital, and head and neck cancers. The central question examines how the cervicovaginal microbiome (CVM) influences HPV infection, persistence, and disease development.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative overview that synthesizes clinical and epidemiological research on the host microbiome as a determinant of HPV pathogenesis. It does not report specific databases, search dates, eligibility criteria, or study counts, nor does it employ a meta-analysis or consensus process.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: There is strong agreement that the host microbiome, particularly the bacterial components of the cervicovaginal microbiome, is a key determinant of HPV infection, persistence, and disease development. High-risk HPVs are established as the primary cause of nearly one-third of all virus-associated cancers worldwide, including cervical and other anogenital cancers.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Challenges in studying HPVs and the microbiome have hindered progress in defining underlying mechanisms, causality, temporal dynamics, and directionality of HPV-CVM interactions. Evidence gaps remain regarding these unresolved aspects and the specific mechanisms through which the CVM influences HPV pathogenesis.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Future research should focus on addressing outstanding questions through emerging in vitro and in vivo models to better understand trans-kingdom interactions contributing to HPV infection and disease. This includes investigating causality, temporal dynamics, and the directionality of the relationship between the CVM and HPV.

analysis.summary_en: This review examines the role of the cervicovaginal microbiome (CVM) as a determinant of human papillomavirus (HPV) infection and disease. High-risk HPVs are established as the cause of nearly one-third of virus-associated cancers, including cervical and other anogenital cancers. While clinical and epidemiological research confirms the CVM's influence on HPV pathogenesis, challenges in studying these interactions have limited progress in defining mechanisms, causality, and temporal dynamics. Emerging models offer opportunities to address these gaps and enhance understanding of trans-kingdom interactions in HPV infection and disease development.

title: A systematic review and meta-analysis of diagnostic accuracy of urine self-sampling for human papillomavirus detection in cervical cancer screening

analysis.scope_and_question: The review evaluates the diagnostic accuracy of urine self-sampling for detecting human papillomavirus (HPV) infections and HPV-associated high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions (HSIL) compared with clinician-collected cervical and vaginal samples in cervical cancer screening programs.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This systematic review followed PRISMA-P guidelines, was registered in PROSPERO (CRD42024511154), and searched PubMed and Embase (January 2013–October 2023) for full-text English studies comparing urine-based HPV testing with provider-collected samples in clinical settings. Risk of bias was assessed using QUADAS-2 and QUADAS-C tools, and a random-effects meta-analysis summarized diagnostic accuracy.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Cervical samples demonstrated the highest diagnostic accuracy for detecting high-risk HPV and HPV-associated HSIL, followed by vaginal samples, while urine samples performed the lowest. Sensitivity for detecting high-risk HPV-HSIL was 75% for urine, compared with 92% for vaginal and 95% for cervical samples. Specificities were comparable between urine (87%) and vaginal samples (88%).
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review highlights reduced sensitivity of urine self-sampling for detecting high-risk HPV and HPV-associated HSIL compared with vaginal and cervical sampling, despite comparable specificities. The lower diagnostic performance of urine samples raises concerns about their reliability for screening purposes.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Urine self-sampling may serve as a non-invasive and acceptable screening option for women who might otherwise not participate, despite its lower sensitivity. Further research is needed to optimize urine-based HPV testing protocols and improve diagnostic accuracy to match or approach the performance of vaginal and cervical sampling methods.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review assessed the diagnostic accuracy of urine self-sampling for human papillomavirus (HPV) detection compared with clinician-collected cervical and vaginal samples in cervical cancer screening. Following PRISMA-P guidelines and PROSPERO registration, the review searched PubMed and Embase (2013–2023) and included 13 studies. Risk of bias was evaluated using QUADAS-2 and QUADAS-C, and a random-effects meta-analysis was conducted. Cervical samples showed the highest diagnostic accuracy for high-risk HPV and HPV-associated HSIL, followed by vaginal samples, while urine samples performed the lowest. Sensitivity for detecting high-risk HPV-HSIL was 75% for urine, 92% for vaginal, and 95% for cervical samples, with specificities of 87% (urine) and 88% (vaginal). Urine self-sampling may offer a non-invasive screening option for under-screened women, though its lower sensitivity necessitates further optimization.

title: Perceived facilitators and barriers against human papillomavirus vaccine among rural parents with eligible daughters in the Alle district, Southern Ethiopia

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study was needed because there are few studies on HPV vaccine acceptance in Ethiopia, with most focusing on quantitative approaches, and it aimed to explore parental perceptions about HPV vaccine acceptance.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A qualitative study using focus group discussions and in-depth interviews was conducted from April 25, 2023, to May 25, 2023, among eligible parents of daughters in the Alle district, southern Ethiopia, with a convenience sample of 53 parents for focus groups and 15 parents for interviews.
analysis.methods: Data were collected using semi-structured focus group discussion guides and in-depth interview questionnaires, translated into English after transcription, and analyzed thematically using Atlas software version 7.1.16.
analysis.main_results: Among participants, 66.2% were female parents and 60.2% were Protestant religious followers, with findings split into perceived facilitators and barriers to HPV vaccine acceptance.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that parents identified various facilitators and barriers to accepting the HPV vaccine, with the study providing qualitative insights into these factors in a rural Ethiopian context.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform targeted interventions to address identified barriers and leverage facilitators, potentially improving HPV vaccine acceptance in rural Ethiopia through collaboration between government and health institutions.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is moderate due to the qualitative design and limited sample size, which may limit generalizability, though the study provides valuable context-specific insights.

analysis.summary_en: This qualitative study explored parental perceptions of HPV vaccine acceptance among rural parents in southern Ethiopia. Conducted through focus groups and interviews with 68 parents, the study identified key facilitators, such as preventing cervical cancer and trusting health professionals, and barriers, including lack of awareness, misinformation, and cultural factors. The findings highlight the need for targeted interventions to improve vaccine uptake, with recommendations for government and health institutions to address these challenges. While the study provides valuable context-specific insights, its qualitative nature and limited sample size moderate the generalizability of the results.

title: Type-specific sensitivity versus detection breadth in HPV diagnostics: improved analytical detection of HPV16/18 by nested PCR

analysis.research_question_and_background: Accurate detection of high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) is central to cervical cancer screening. Current diagnostic strategies increasingly prioritize broad-spectrum assays to maximize genotype coverage.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study evaluated the analytical trade-off between type-specific sensitivity and detection breadth using conventional PCR as a controlled experimental framework. Type-specific nested PCR assays targeting HPV16 and HPV18 were developed and applied to 41 cervical samples.
analysis.methods: Nested PCR showed markedly higher relative analytical sensitivity than single-round amplification and produced a greater proportion of specific and interpretable detections than the broad-spectrum consensus systems tested here (MY09/11 and GP5/6).
analysis.main_results: HPV16 and/or HPV18 DNA was detected by nested PCR in 22/41 samples, whereas MY09/11 and GP5/6 detected 11/41 and 2/41 samples, respectively, under the tested conditions.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: These findings indicate that broad genotype coverage and effective detection of positive samples are distinct analytical properties.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results support explicit preservation of per-target analytical sensitivity in reflex testing and future multi-target HPV assay design.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to 41 cervical samples, and the results are not intended to replace clinically validated broad-spectrum screening assays.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the analytical trade-off between type-specific sensitivity and detection breadth in HPV diagnostics. It evaluates the effectiveness of nested PCR assays targeting HPV16 and HPV18 compared to broad-spectrum consensus systems (MY09/11 and GP5/6) in detecting HPV in cervical samples. The results show that nested PCR has higher sensitivity for HPV16 and HPV18 than the consensus methods, detecting DNA in 22/41 samples versus 11/41 and 2/41 for the other systems. The findings highlight that broad genotype coverage and effective detection of positive samples are distinct properties, suggesting that genotype-focused assays may be more effective in settings where prevalent HPV targets occur at low abundance. The study supports the need to preserve per-target analytical sensitivity in reflex testing and future multi-target HPV assay design, but it does not replace clinically validated broad-spectrum screening assays.

title: Occupational human papillomavirus exposure risks for laryngeal surgeons and phoniatricians: A joint European Laryngological Society (ELS) and Union of European Phoniatricians (UEP) Delphi clinical consensus statement

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to address the occupational human papillomavirus (HPV) exposure risks for laryngeal surgeons and phoniatricians, focusing on surgical smoke as a potential source of viral transmission during procedures like recurrent respiratory papillomatosis management.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A modified Delphi consensus process was conducted under the auspices of the European Laryngological Society (ELS) and the Union of the European Phoniatricians (UEP), involving 26 international experts across three rounds of voting.
analysis.methods: The panel evaluated 18 statements across five domains (definitions and risk perception, personal protective measures, smoke evacuation and ventilation, preventive vaccination, and areas for further research) through iterative voting and consensus-building.
analysis.main_results: All panellists completed all three rounds; of the 18 statements, one reached strong consensus, seven reached consensus, one reached near consensus, and six did not reach consensus, with three statements merged across rounds.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: This joint ELS and UEP consensus statement represents the first internationally coordinated effort to address occupational HPV exposure in laryngology, highlighting key areas of agreement and remaining uncertainties.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings emphasize the need for targeted research, consistent protective measures, educational provision, and regulatory frameworks to mitigate occupational HPV exposure risks in healthcare settings.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is moderate, as the study relies on expert consensus rather than empirical data, though the Delphi method provides a structured approach to synthesizing expert opinions.

analysis.summary_en: This study developed an evidence-informed clinical consensus statement to guide occupational HPV risk management in laryngology, addressing concerns about surgical smoke as a potential source of viral exposure. Using a modified Delphi process with 26 international experts, the panel evaluated 18 statements across five domains, achieving consensus on key areas including the recognition of surgical smoke as a risk, the inadequacy of standard masks, and the importance of HPV vaccination for healthcare workers. While the findings represent a first internationally coordinated effort, they also underscore the need for further research and consistent protective measures. The evidence strength is moderate, reflecting the consensus-based approach rather than empirical data.

title: Attitudes and Knowledge About Human Papillomavirus and Cervical Cancer among Women Referred to a Tertiary Gynecologic Oncology Clinic, Tehran, Iran

analysis.research_question_and_background: Cervical cancer is a major public health concern worldwide. This study aimed to assess the attitudes and knowledge about Human Papillomavirus (HPV) and cervical cancer among women attending a tertiary gynecologic clinic.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This descriptive, cross-sectional survey was conducted among 139 women referred to the gynecologic clinics of Yas Hospital Complex, affiliated with Tehran University of Medical Sciences, from 2023 to 2024.
analysis.methods: Data were collected through face-to-face interviews. Data analysis was performed using SPSS (IBM SPSS Statistics for Windows, Version 25).
analysis.main_results: The mean total knowledge score was 25.07±5.92 out of a possible 33 points. Educational attainment was significantly associated with knowledge levels (P=0.01).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Participants demonstrated strong foundational awareness, correctly identifying HPV as a sexually transmitted infection, recognizing that HPV affects both genders, and recognizing its role in causing cervical cancer.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings highlight an urgent need for educational interventions targeting these knowledge gaps, particularly among women with lower educational attainment.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report limitations of the study. The evidence strength is moderate due to the cross-sectional design and potential for self-reporting bias.

analysis.summary_en: This study assessed the attitudes and knowledge about Human Papillomavirus (HPV) and cervical cancer among 139 women attending a tertiary gynecologic clinic in Tehran, Iran, between 2023 and 2024. Data were collected through face-to-face interviews and analyzed using SPSS. The mean total knowledge score was 25.07±5.92 out of 33 points, indicating strong foundational awareness of HPV as a sexually transmitted infection and its role in cervical cancer. However, knowledge of the risks of vertical transmission and the lack of a specific antiviral treatment for HPV was low. Educational attainment was significantly associated with knowledge levels (P=0.01), and it was the strongest predictor of knowledge scores. The study underscores the need for targeted educational interventions to address misconceptions about HPV and cervical cancer, especially among women with lower educational backgrounds. The evidence strength is moderate due to the cross-sectional design and potential for self-reporting bias.

title: Association of vaginal dysbiosis with cervical lesions among women with non-16/18 high-risk HPV infections: a cross-sectional study of 2,264 women in Eastern China

analysis.research_question_and_background: To investigate whether vaginal dysbiosis is associated with an increased risk of cervical lesions infected with non-16/18 high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) genotypes and to inform risk-stratified cervical cancer screening strategies.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This cross‐sectional study included 2,264 women attending Jiaxing Maternal and Child Health Hospital between June 2023 and October 2024.
analysis.methods: HPV genotyping, vaginal microecological assessment, and Thinprep cytologic test (TCT) were performed. Logistic regression models were used to evaluate associations, adjusting for age. Multiplicative interaction was assessed using Wald tests for product terms, and Benjamini‐Hochberg FDR correction was applied for multiple comparisons.
analysis.main_results: The overall HPV prevalence was 49.87%, with HR-HPV detected in 36.13%. HR‐HPV infection was significantly associated with cervical lesions in both normal (OR = 11.45) and dysbiotic (OR = 4.40) vaginal microbiota (both P < 0.001). Stratified analyses showed higher point estimates for HPV58 and HPV59 in the dysbiosis group (OR = 10.98 and 9.51, respectively) than in the normal group (OR = 7.50 and 6.44, respectively), but formal multiplicative interaction tests did not reach statistical significance (Wald P = 0.526 and 0.559, respectively; FDR‐adjusted q = 0.559 for both). No HPV subtype remained significantly associated with ASC‐US after FDR correction.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: In this cross‐sectional study, vaginal dysbiosis is specifically associated with cervical lesions among women with non‐16/18 HR-HPV infections, particularly HPV58 and HPV59, which showed elevated point estimates in the presence of dysbiosis. However, formal multiplicative interaction tests did not reach statistical significance, and the findings are exploratory and hypothesis‐generating; causality cannot be inferred due to the cross‐sectional design.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings may inform risk-stratified cervical cancer screening strategies, particularly for women with non-16/18 HR-HPV infections and vaginal dysbiosis, but prospective studies are needed to validate the observed associations before any clinical application can be considered. The results should be interpreted with caution and do not support changes to current screening practice.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The cross‐sectional design limits causal inference, and the exploratory nature of the findings requires validation in prospective studies. The evidence strength is moderate due to the large sample size and rigorous statistical adjustments, but the lack of significant interaction tests and the cross-sectional design reduce confidence in establishing causality.

analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study investigated the association between vaginal dysbiosis and cervical lesions in women with non-16/18 high-risk HPV infections in Eastern China. Among 2,264 women, HR-HPV prevalence was 36.13%, and dysbiosis was associated with higher odds of cervical lesions, particularly for HPV58 and HPV59. However, formal interaction tests were not significant, and the cross-sectional design limits causal inference. The findings are exploratory and do not support changes to current screening practices, highlighting the need for prospective validation.

title: Effects of a Message‐Framing Video Intervention on Maternal Vaccine Confidence Regarding HPV Vaccination for Daughters: A Quasi‐Experimental Study Among Mothers With Cervical Intraepithelial Neoplasia

analysis.research_question_and_background: Increasing HPV vaccination coverage is pivotal, necessitating effective vaccination strategies. This research assessed the impact of a message‐framing video intervention on boosting vaccine confidence among mothers diagnosed with cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN), targeting HPV vaccination for their daughters.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Conducted from January to June 2024, this interventional study took place at the gynecological cervical clinic of a university‐affiliated hospital and targeted CIN patients from adjacent communities. Mothers with daughters aged 9–14 years, who were unvaccinated and whose mothers were diagnosed with CIN, participated.
analysis.methods: They were allocated to receive either standard health education or a targeted message‐framing video intervention. Outcome data were collected by trained researchers after a 10‐week intervention period, focusing on maternal knowledge, attitudes, and behaviors toward their daughters’ HPV vaccination.
analysis.main_results: A total of 101 patients were analyzed. Those exposed to the message‐framing video intervention exhibited significantly improved knowledge, attitudes, and behaviors towards HPV vaccination (Z = −3.376, P = 0.001), and demonstrated lower vaccine hesitancy scores (Z = −2.924, P = 0.003) compared to their counterparts receiving standard health education. However, differences in the rates of scheduling vaccine appointments were not statistically significant between the groups (χ2 = 0.934, P = 0.334).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The message‐framing video intervention significantly enhanced vaccine confidence by improving the knowledge and willingness of CIN patients to vaccinate their daughters against HPV. Further studies are required to explore the intervention's influence on actual vaccination rates.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that message‐framing interventions can be effective in improving vaccine confidence among high-risk populations, potentially contributing to increased HPV vaccination coverage. analysis.study_design_and_population: This was a multicenter cross-sectional study conducted within a cervical cancer screening program in China, enrolling 3,077 high-risk HPV-positive women between the study dates.
analysis.methods: HPV integration was detected using high-throughput viral integration detection (HIVID), and multivariable logistic regression and structural equation modeling (SEM) were used to assess associations and mediating effects between HPV 16/18, HPV integration, and CIN3+.
analysis.main_results: HPV 16/18 prevalence was 29.5%, HPV integration prevalence was 12.9%, and CIN3+ prevalence was 5.9%. Both HPV integration and HPV 16/18 were independently associated with CIN3+ in multivariable analysis.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study demonstrates that HPV integration mediates 78.1% of the total effect of HPV 16/18 on CIN3+, providing new evidence that HPV integration status may refine risk stratification for CIN3+ in HPV-positive women.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that incorporating HPV integration testing into cervical cancer screening could improve identification of women at highest risk for CIN3+, potentially guiding more targeted clinical management and follow-up.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: As a cross-sectional study, temporality cannot be established, limiting causal inference; the evidence strength is moderate given the single-country setting and reliance on screening-program data.

analysis.summary_en: This multicenter cross-sectional study in China evaluated 3,077 high-risk HPV-positive women to investigate whether HPV integration mediates the association between HPV 16/18 and CIN3+. Using HIVID for integration detection and SEM for mediation analysis, the authors found that both HPV integration and HPV 16/18 were independently associated with CIN3+, and that HPV integration accounted for 78.1% of the total effect of HPV 16/18 on CIN3+. The study interprets these results as evidence that HPV integration status could refine risk stratification for CIN3+ in HPV-positive women, offering new insights for clinical translation of integration testing within cervical cancer screening programs.

title: Orientation of Gp96 and Calreticulin T-cell epitopes in a multiepitope HPV16 E7 vaccine construct affects predicted immunostimulatory properties: An in silico and expression validation study

analysis.research_question_and_background: Heat shock proteins (HSPs) can be used as adjuvants to develop therapeutic vaccines, as they enhance the cross-presentation of related tumor antigens and stimulate T cells. analysis.methods: In silico evaluation was performed to select epitopes from HSPs based on high binding affinity to MHC-I/II, strong immunogenicity, and population coverage. The multiepitope gp96-CRT-E7 fusion peptide was expressed in the Rosetta strain under specific conditions and purified through affinity chromatography.
analysis.main_results: Our data showed that the gp96-CRT-E7 construct had superior docking scores with receptors (especially TLR2 and LOX-1), suggesting stronger stimulation of both innate and adaptive immunity than other constructs. It was predicted to be non-toxic, non-allergenic, antigenic, immunogenic, and structurally stable. Generally, successful results of in silico and expression validation of the multiepitope gp96-CRT-E7 fusion peptide showed its strong potential as a novel candidate for HPV16 vaccine development.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The orientation of Gp96 and Calreticulin T-cell epitopes in a multiepitope HPV16 E7 vaccine construct affects predicted immunostimulatory properties, with the gp96-CRT-E7 construct demonstrating superior immunostimulatory potential. analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to in silico predictions and expression validation in a prokaryotic system, without in vivo or clinical evaluation. analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the immunostimulatory properties of gp96 and calreticulin to enhance HPV16 E7-based vaccine effectiveness. The construct was predicted to be non-toxic, non-allergenic, antigenic, immunogenic, and structurally stable. Successful expression and purification of the multiepitope gp96-CRT-E7 fusion peptide in a prokaryotic system validated its potential as a novel candidate for HPV16 vaccine development. This approach may contribute to improved immunotherapy strategies for HPV-related diseases, though further in vivo and clinical evaluations are needed.

title: Data from Tissue Context Shapes Distinct Premalignant Outcomes in an HPV16 E6/E7-Mutant Pik3ca Transgenic Mouse Model

analysis.methods: Histopathological analysis and immunohistochemistry (IHC) were performed to assess dysplastic changes, E6 expression, and markers like K14, K7, and pS6 in the anal mucosa of transgenic and control mice.
analysis.main_results: TG-E6/E7 mice developed low-grade (LSIL) and high-grade (HSIL) squamous intraepithelial lesions in the anal mucosa, with E6 expression localized to basal and suprabasal layers, while controls showed no lesions or E6 expression.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that tissue-specific factors in the anal canal drive distinct premalignant outcomes, with E6/E7 expression sufficient to induce lesions, and the study demonstrated the model's utility for studying HPV-associated carcinogenesis.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings provide insights into HPV-driven carcinogenesis mechanisms and may inform surveillance and prevention strategies for HPV-associated anal lesions in humans.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is moderate due to the limited sample size and reliance on a single animal model, though the study provides detailed histopathological and molecular data.

The study demonstrates the model's utility for studying HPV-associated carcinogenesis and provides insights into tissue-specific mechanisms of HPV-driven lesions, with potential implications for human HPV-related disease prevention and surveillance.

title: NFX1-123 is required for keratinocyte differentiation and HPV 16 DNA maintenance in early and persistent infection models

analysis.research_question_and_background: Persistent high-risk human papillomavirus (HR HPV) infections cause nearly 5% of cancers worldwide, including cervical and oropharyngeal cancers. The study aimed to investigate the role of NFX1-123 abundance on the initiation and persistence of HPV 16 infections.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study utilized keratinocytes with overexpressed, endogenous, or reduced levels of NFX1-123 and infected these cells with an HPV 16 quasivirus (Qsv) to model both early and persistent infection.
analysis.methods: Keratinocytes with modulated NFX1-123 levels were infected with HPV 16 Qsv, and changes to keratinocyte growth and viral DNA copy numbers were analyzed in monolayer and three-dimensional raft cultures.
analysis.main_results: Keratinocytes with reduced NFX1-123 had blunted differentiation and stratification in raft cultures, correlating with decreased HPV 16 Qsv DNA copies. Similarly, reducing NFX1-123 in W12E cells decreased raft culture differentiation, thickness, and viral genome copies.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings indicate that NFX1-123 is required for keratinocyte differentiation and stratification, and its disruption significantly impairs HPV 16's ability to maintain its episomal genome at consistent copy numbers.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings highlight the importance of NFX1-123 for the persistence of HPV 16 infections and suggest it as a potential therapeutic target in HPV 16-positive cancers and precancers.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was conducted in vitro using keratinocyte models, which may not fully replicate in vivo conditions. The evidence strength is moderate due to the use of cell culture models and the need for further validation in vivo.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the role of the host protein NFX1-123 in HPV 16 infection persistence. Using keratinocytes with modulated NFX1-123 levels and HPV 16 quasivirus, the researchers found that reduced NFX1-123 impairs keratinocyte differentiation and stratification in raft cultures, correlating with decreased viral DNA copies. Similarly, reducing NFX1-123 in W12E cells, a cervical cell line with episomal HPV 16 genomes, led to decreased differentiation and fewer viral copies. These findings demonstrate that NFX1-123 is essential for HPV 16 genome maintenance and suggest it as a potential therapeutic target for HPV-associated cancers.

title: Efficacy of live lactobacillus preparations in treating cervical inflammation and clearing viral infections in patients with HPV infection complicated by bacterial vaginosis

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of Dingjunsheng, a live Lactobacillus preparation, as adjuvant therapy in patients with human papillomavirus (HPV) infection complicated by bacterial vaginosis (BV).
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective analysis was conducted on 152 eligible patients, randomly divided into two groups: the observation group (n=87) receiving standard BV antibacterial therapy plus Dingjunsheng, and the control group (n=65) who received standard BV antibacterial therapy alone. The patients were followed up for six months.
analysis.methods: Primary outcomes included HPV clearance rate and cervical cytological inflammation improvement, while secondary outcomes involved BV recurrence rate and adverse reaction incidence.
analysis.main_results: The results showed that the observation group had a significantly higher HPV clearance rate (73.6% vs 53.9%) and inflammation improvement rate (90.8% vs 76.9%), as well as a lower BV recurrence rate (3.1% vs 13.9%) compared to the control group. Dingjunsheng was identified as an independent protective factor for HPV clearance (OR=2.5, 95%CI:1.3–5.1).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors concluded that Dingjunsheng adjuvant therapy demonstrated effectiveness in improving HPV clearance, alleviating inflammation, and reducing BV recurrence, with good safety, making it a valuable treatment strategy for these patients.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that Dingjunsheng as an adjuvant therapy could improve outcomes in patients with HPV infection complicated by BV, potentially reducing recurrence rates and enhancing viral clearance.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was a retrospective analysis, which may introduce selection bias. The evidence strength is moderate due to the study design and sample size.

analysis.summary_en: This retrospective study evaluated the efficacy of Dingjunsheng, a live Lactobacillus preparation, as adjuvant therapy in 152 patients with HPV infection complicated by bacterial vaginosis. Patients were divided into an observation group receiving standard therapy plus Dingjunsheng (n=87) and a control group receiving standard therapy alone (n=65), followed for six months. The observation group showed significantly higher HPV clearance (73.6% vs 53.9%), inflammation improvement (90.8% vs 76.9%), and lower BV recurrence (3.1% vs 13.9%). Dingjunsheng was identified as an independent protective factor for HPV clearance (OR=2.5, 95%CI:1.3–5.1). Adverse reaction rates were similar between groups. The study suggests Dingjunsheng is a safe and effective adjuvant therapy for these patients.

title: Prevalence and behavioral factors associated with penile and rectal HPV infection among men who have sex with men in Kenya

analysis.research_question_and_background: High-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) is a leading cause of anogenital cancers and disproportionately affects men who have sex with men (MSM), particularly in low- and middle-income countries. Few studies in sub-Saharan Africa have concurrently examined penile and rectal hrHPV infection and their site-specific behavioral and biological correlates.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of baseline data from MSM aged 18–35 years in Kisumu, Kenya. Clinician-collected penile and rectal swabs were tested for hrHPV using the ScreenFire HPV assay.
analysis.methods: Urine and rectal specimens were tested for Chlamydia trachomatis and Neisseria gonorrhoeae using GeneXpert, and HIV status was confirmed as per Kenyan national guidelines. Log-binomial regression was used to estimate adjusted prevalence ratios (aPR) for associations with sociodemographic, behavioral, and biological factors.
analysis.main_results: Penile hrHPV prevalence was 24.7% (39/158) and rectal hrHPV prevalence was 12.5% (22/176); 6.7% of participants tested at both sites had dual-site infection. HPV-18/45 was the most common genotype group at both sites. Penile hrHPV was more likely among participants with HIV (aPR = 2.27, p = 0.050) and less common among employed participants (aPR = 0.25, p = 0.048).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that hrHPV infection was common among MSM in Kisumu, Kenya, with distinct site-specific correlates. The strong association between rectal bacterial STIs and rectal hrHPV highlights the need for integrated HPV and STI screening.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings support expansion of gender-neutral HPV vaccination and etiologic STI screening to reduce HPV-associated cancer risk among MSM in sub-Saharan Africa. Integrated screening could improve early detection and prevention of HPV-related diseases in this high-risk population.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was cross-sectional, limiting causal inference. The evidence strength is moderate due to the sample size and potential confounding factors, but the findings are consistent with biological plausibility and prior research.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the prevalence and behavioral factors associated with penile and rectal hrHPV infection among MSM in Kisumu, Kenya. A cross-sectional analysis of 158-176 participants aged 18-35 years found penile hrHPV prevalence at 24.7% and rectal hrHPV at 12.5%, with HPV-18/45 as the most common genotype. Key correlates included HIV status for penile infection and rectal bacterial STIs for rectal infection. The authors concluded that hrHPV is common with site-specific factors, supporting integrated HPV and STI screening and gender-neutral vaccination to reduce cancer risk in this population. The cross-sectional design limits causal inference, but the evidence strength is moderate.

title: High-Risk Cervical Human Papillomavirus Prevalence in a Northeast Nigeria Community: A Descriptive Study.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Disparities in cervical screening result in disproportionate cervical cancer burdens in populations. This study assessed cervical human papillomavirus (HPV) infection prevalence in a rural northeast Nigeria community with low access to cervical screening.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A community health outreach was conducted at a primary healthcare facility in Azare, Bauchi State, Nigeria. The women who wished to and consented to undergo gynaecological consultations were non-randomly enrolled on the study and provided their sociodemographic data and cervical specimens.
analysis.methods: These specimens were analysed cytologically and for the presence of HPV deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA).
analysis.main_results: Of 62 women screened (mean age 38.5 ± 9.8 years), 34 (54.8%) tested positive for HPV DNA (95% confidence interval = 43-67%). Among these positive cases, 19 had no intraepithelial lesion or malignancy (NILM), 8 were designated atypical squamous cell of undetermined significance (ASCUS), and 6 showed low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (LSIL). In contrast, one case was high-grade SIL (HSIL).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The results suggest a high prevalence of cervical HR-HPV and SIL in Azare. Improved public enlightenment and access to cervical cancer screening services may help to decrease transmission of HPV and subsequent cervical cancer in the population.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings highlight the urgent need for increased cervical cancer screening and public health education in underserved communities like Azare, Nigeria, to reduce HPV transmission and associated cervical cancer risks.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was limited by its non-random enrollment and small sample size, which may affect generalizability. The evidence strength is moderate due to the descriptive nature and lack of a control group.

analysis.summary_en: This descriptive study assessed cervical human papillomavirus (HPV) infection prevalence in a rural northeast Nigeria community with low access to screening. Among 62 women screened, 54.8% tested positive for HPV DNA, with HPV 16 and 18 being the most common genotypes. Most positive cases showed no lesions or low-grade abnormalities, but one high-grade SIL case was identified. The study highlights a high burden of HR-HPV and SIL, emphasizing the need for improved screening access and public health education to reduce cervical cancer risks in this underserved population.

title: HPV vaccination intention and its association with vaccine hesitancy and health beliefs among unvaccinated Chinese medical college students: A cross-sectional study

analysis.research_question_and_background: Human papillomavirus (HPV) infection poses a significant public health challenge, and HPV vaccination uptake among Chinese college students remains suboptimal.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional survey was conducted from June 16 to July 16, 2024, to assess sociodemographic characteristics, vaccine hesitancy, and health belief model (HBM) among college students at Guangdong Medical University.
analysis.methods: Descriptive statistics, univariate analysis, and binary logistic regression were performed to identify factors associated with HPV vaccination intentions among unvaccinated students.
analysis.main_results: Among 3,584 unvaccinated participants, 73.16% expressed willingness to receive the HPV vaccine.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The key significant associations identified included gender (male) (OR: 0.26; 95% CI: 0.22 ~ 0.31; p < 0.001), parental occupation (employees in enterprises, commercial, and service industries (including self-employed)) (OR: 1.43; 95% CI: 1.18 ~ 1.75; p < 0.001), and information sources (hospitals or doctors) (OR: 1.37; 95% CI: 1.15 ~ 1.64; p = 0.001).
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Vaccination intention was also directly associated with the perceived necessity (OR: 0.91; 95% CI: 0.88 ~ 0.94; p < 0.001) and importance (OR: 1.07; 95% CI: 1.03 ~ 1.10; p < 0.001) of vaccine hesitancy, as well as the perceived benefits of behavior for the HBM (OR: 1.21; 95% CI: 1.12 ~ 1.32; p < 0.001).
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: In this sample, Chinese medical college students demonstrated a relatively high willingness to receive HPV vaccination.

analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study investigated HPV vaccination intention and its association with vaccine hesitancy and health beliefs among unvaccinated Chinese medical college students. Conducted at Guangdong Medical University between June and July 2024, the study used descriptive statistics, univariate analysis, and binary logistic regression to identify factors influencing vaccination intention. Among 3,584 participants, 73.16% expressed willingness to receive the HPV vaccine. Key associations included gender, parental occupation, and information sources. The study highlights the importance of perceived necessity, importance, and benefits of vaccination in shaping intention. The findings suggest that targeted interventions, such as clinician-delivered counseling and gender-neutral policies, may improve vaccine uptake. However, the study is limited to a single institution and may not be generalizable to all populations.

analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Primary HPV testing is now the preferred screening method recommended by the American Cancer Society and anticipated to be endorsed by the United States Preventive Services Task Force, due to its high sensitivity in detecting high-risk HPV.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review does not explicitly discuss controversies or evidence gaps, focusing instead on the transition to primary HPV testing and its institutional impact.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The implications include the need for logistical adjustments in cytopathology laboratories to accommodate increased specimen volumes and the development of triage strategies for HPV-positive cases.

analysis.summary_en: This review examines the historical evolution of cervical cancer screening, highlighting the shift from cytology-based approaches to primary HPV testing as the preferred method. It discusses the etiologic role of high-risk HPV in cervical cancer and outlines the logistical requirements for implementing primary HPV screening, including triage strategies. The authors present institutional experience, noting the impact on laboratory workflow and specimen volumes. The review emphasizes the endorsement of primary HPV testing by major guidelines and anticipates further adoption, though it does not address controversies or evidence gaps.

title: The oral microbiota in oral squamous cell carcinoma: unravelling mechanisms and clinical potential

analysis.scope_and_question: This review focuses on the oral microbiota in oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC), examining its role in carcinogenesis mechanisms and clinical potential. The central question involves understanding how microbial dysbiosis contributes to OSCC initiation and progression.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review provides an integrated overview of the oral microbiome in OSCC, focusing on composition, protective roles, stability factors, and carcinogenesis mechanisms. It also discusses microbiome-targeted strategies as potential adjunctive approaches.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: There is consensus that oral microbial dysbiosis contributes to OSCC initiation and progression. Pathogenic bacteria like Porphyromonas gingivalis and Treponema denticola activate oncogenic pathways, while high-risk HPV and Candida albicans act as cofactors. The oral microbiome is recognized as a source of non-invasive biomarkers.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review does not explicitly mention controversies or evidence gaps, but it highlights the need for further research on microbiome-targeted strategies and the specific mechanisms by which different microbial components contribute to carcinogenesis.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests microbiome-targeted strategies, including prebiotics, probiotics, and postbiotics, as promising adjunctive approaches to restore microbial balance and reduce tumor-promoting inflammation. It also emphasizes the potential of the oral microbiome as a source of non-invasive biomarkers.

analysis.summary_en: This review examines the oral microbiota's role in oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC), highlighting how microbial dysbiosis contributes to carcinogenesis. It discusses the shift toward pathogenic bacterial communities, such as Porphyromonas gingivalis, which activate oncogenic pathways, and the involvement of high-risk HPV and Candida albicans as cofactors. The review emphasizes the oral microbiome's potential as a source of non-invasive biomarkers and proposes microbiome-targeted strategies like prebiotics, probiotics, and postbiotics to restore balance and reduce inflammation. The integrated overview provides insights into mechanisms and clinical applications for OSCC management.

title: Evaluating the feasibility of using SMS to recruit women for cervical cancer screening in Rwanda: A pilot study.

analysis.scope_and_question: This study evaluates the feasibility and acceptability of using short message service (SMS) as a recruitment strategy for cervical cancer screening in an urban sector of Kigali, Rwanda.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This pilot invited 300 women who had not attended cervical screening during the local campaign and had access to a mobile phone to provide a mobile number for cervical cancer screening invitation. Up to three SMSs were sent out, inviting women to visit a local health center for cervical cancer screening. There, attendance rates were recorded, self-collected vaginal samples for human papillomavirus testing were taken, and a short survey was administered. Those who did not attend received a phone call and were surveyed on reasons for non-attendance. A descriptive analysis was used to detail attendance rates and evaluate survey questions on the perceived feasibility and acceptability of the intervention.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: A total of 294 women met the inclusion criteria. Of these women, 86.4% (254/294) attended the health center for cervical cancer screening and 92.9% (236/254) of attendees reported they participated due to the SMS reminder. Survey items evaluating acceptability and feasibility indicated high message comprehension, strong attendance following a single SMS prompt, and high agreement that SMS was a helpful reminder to attend screening.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Most non-attendees reported having received the SMSs but not attending due to circumstantial factors. Future research should aim to understand the efficacy of this strategy compared to usual recruitment methods across diverse settings in Rwanda.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: SMS recruitment was highly feasible and well accepted in this pilot study in an urban sector of Kigali, Rwanda.

analysis.summary_en: This pilot study assesses the feasibility and acceptability of using SMS to recruit women for cervical cancer screening in an urban area of Kigali, Rwanda. The study invited 300 women who had not attended screening during a local campaign and had mobile phone access. Up to three SMSs were sent to encourage attendance, and a short survey was administered to evaluate perceptions of the intervention. A total of 294 women met the inclusion criteria, with 86.4% attending the health center and 92.9% of attendees citing SMS as the reason for participation. Survey results indicated high comprehension, strong attendance following a single SMS prompt, and positive feedback on SMS as a reminder. Non-attendees reported receiving SMSs but not attending due to circumstantial factors. The study concludes that SMS recruitment was highly feasible and well accepted in this setting. It suggests that future research should explore the efficacy of SMS compared to traditional recruitment methods in different contexts within Rwanda.

title: Health economic impact and cost threshold for switching from bivalent to nonavalent HPV vaccination for preadolescent girls in KwaZulu Natal, South Africa: A mathematical modeling analysis accounting for the HIV epidemic.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the cost-effectiveness and cost threshold for switching from bivalent to nonavalent HPV vaccination in preadolescent girls in KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa, accounting for the HIV epidemic, given that 9vHPV could avert more cervical cancer burden but its cost-effectiveness in this setting was unknown.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A mathematical modeling analysis was conducted using a validated compartmental HPV and HIV transmission model parameterized to KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa, simulating scenarios of 2vHPV and 9vHPV implementation over 100 years with varying coverage and dosing strategies.
analysis.methods: The study simulated vaccination scenarios with two doses (72% coverage) and one dose (80% and 90% coverage) with lifelong or waning single-dose vaccine efficacy, evaluated cervical cancer cases and deaths averted, and estimated the maximum cost/dose for 9vHPV to be cost-effective using willingness-to-pay thresholds from $500 to $3,015/DALY averted.
analysis.main_results: Single-dose 9vHPV at 80% coverage could avert 7.9% more cervical cancer cases and 6.4% more deaths than 2vHPV (lifelong efficacy), with the maximum cost-effective 9vHPV price ranging from $15 to $45/dose depending on the threshold; at current costs ($110/dose), single-dose 9vHPV at 90% coverage exceeded cost-effective thresholds with ICERs of $10,480/DALY averted (lifelong efficacy) and $8,806/DALY averted (waning efficacy).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that implementing 9vHPV can result in a greater reduction in cervical cancer burden than 2vHPV, but vaccine costs need to be reduced for 9vHPV to be cost-effective in KwaZulu-Natal, with the novelty being the cost-threshold analysis specific to this high-HIV-prevalence setting.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform vaccination policy in South Africa by providing evidence that switching to 9vHPV could reduce cervical cancer burden but requires cost reductions to be cost-effective, guiding future procurement decisions and resource allocation for HPV vaccination programs in similar settings.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is moderate due to the reliance on mathematical modeling rather than real-world data, with limitations including the uncertainty around long-term vaccine efficacy and the model's assumptions about HIV-HPV interactions, though the use of a validated parameterized model enhances credibility.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the cost-effectiveness of switching from bivalent to nonavalent HPV vaccination in preadolescent girls in KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa, using a mathematical model accounting for the HIV epidemic. The analysis found that single-dose 9vHPV at 80% coverage could avert 7.9% more cervical cancer cases and 6.4% more deaths than 2vHPV, but the maximum cost-effective price for 9vHPV ranged from $15 to $45/dose depending on the willingness-to-pay threshold. At current costs, 9vHPV at 90% coverage exceeded cost-effective thresholds. The study concludes that while 9vHPV could reduce cervical cancer burden more effectively, cost reductions are necessary for it to be cost-effective in this setting, providing critical evidence for vaccination policy decisions in high-HIV-prevalence regions.

title: HPV vaccination and the risk of cancer in males

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the lack of evidence regarding the relationship between HPV vaccination in males and the risk of potentially HPV-associated cancers beyond head and neck cancer.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective cohort study was conducted using the TriNetX United States Collaborative Network, including males aged 9 to 45 years who did or did not receive the HPV vaccine between 2006 and 2024.
analysis.methods: The study assessed the association between HPV vaccination and the risk of cancer, carcinoma in situ, and precancerous lesions at multiple anatomical sites using hazard ratio analysis.
analysis.main_results: Males with HPV vaccination (n = 397,856) had a lower hazard ratio for head and neck cancer, as well as for lung cancer, prostate cancer, and colorectal cancer; vaccinated males were also less likely to develop precancerous lesions of the anus, head and neck, esophagus, and stomach.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that HPV vaccination significantly reduces the risk of certain cancers and precancerous lesions in males, representing a novel finding beyond established associations with cervical cancer in females and head and neck cancer in males.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings support the expansion of HPV vaccination recommendations to males for the prevention of a broader range of HPV-associated cancers and precancerous lesions, potentially reducing cancer burden and healthcare costs.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Further studies are needed to evaluate the protective mechanisms of HPV vaccination against various cancers; the evidence strength is moderate due to the retrospective design and the need for additional mechanistic research.

analysis.summary_en: This retrospective cohort study investigated the association between HPV vaccination and cancer risk in males aged 9 to 45 years using the TriNetX United States Collaborative Network. Among 397,856 vaccinated males, significantly lower hazard ratios were observed for head and neck cancer, as well as for lung, prostate, and colorectal cancers. Vaccinated males also showed reduced risk of precancerous lesions in the anus, head and neck, esophagus, and stomach. The findings demonstrate that HPV vaccination significantly reduces the risk of multiple potentially HPV-associated cancers and precancerous lesions in males, extending beyond the previously established benefits for cervical cancer in females and head and neck cancer in males. While the results support broader vaccination recommendations, further research is needed to elucidate the protective mechanisms against various cancers.

title: Insights of Vietnamese American Women on Cervical Cancer Screening and HPV Self-Sampling

analysis.research_question_and_background: Vietnamese American women experience one of the highest cervical cancer incidence and mortality rates in the United States, largely due to low screening uptake. To inform strategies for reducing this burden, we explored the experiences and attitudes toward cervical cancer screening, including the perceptions on Human papillomavirus (HPV) self-sampling, among Vietnamese American women.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Between April 2023 and July 2024, we conducted four focus groups and three individual interviews with 21 Vietnamese American women aged 30–65 residing in Southern California. Participants were stratified by nativity and age: Vietnam-born ages 30–49, Vietnam-born ages 50–65, and U.S.-born ages 30–49.
analysis.methods: All focus groups and interviews were conducted online and moderated by a bilingual researcher using semi-structured guides. Participants also watched videos on screening methods and shared their views. The discussions were recorded, transcribed, and thematically analyzed using Dedoose 10.0.59.
analysis.main_results: Three themes emerged, with no differences across strata. First, structural and psychosocial barriers to physician-based screening were identified. Second, HPV self-sampling was viewed as a potential solution to these barriers, though there were mixed opinions regarding one's ability to self-sample correctly, potential discomfort, and logistics related to obtaining a device and mailing samples. Third, other opportunities to improve screening uptake were identified, including a high willingness to undergo screening, the potential to capitalize on the strong trust in physicians, and the opportunities to leverage community-based resources.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Our findings suggest that a multifaceted approach integrating HPV self-sampling and provider and community engagement has the potential to improve cervical cancer screening uptake among Vietnamese American women.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study highlights the potential of HPV self-sampling as a solution to barriers in cervical cancer screening uptake among Vietnamese American women, emphasizing the need for provider and community engagement to improve screening rates.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was limited by its small sample size and qualitative design, which may limit generalizability. However, the thematic analysis provided rich insights into the experiences and attitudes of Vietnamese American women toward cervical cancer screening and HPV self-sampling.

analysis.summary_en: This study explored the experiences and attitudes of Vietnamese American women toward cervical cancer screening and HPV self-sampling. Conducted between April 2023 and July 2024, the research involved four focus groups and three individual interviews with 21 Vietnamese American women aged 30–65 in Southern California. The participants were stratified by nativity and age. The study identified three main themes: structural and psychosocial barriers to physician-based screening, HPV self-sampling as a potential solution with mixed opinions, and opportunities to improve screening uptake through provider and community engagement. The findings suggest that a multifaceted approach integrating HPV self-sampling and community-based strategies could enhance cervical cancer screening rates among Vietnamese American women.

title: Opportunities and Barriers to HPV Vaccination Among Men Who Have Sex with Men and Related Sexual and Gender Minority Populations: A Systematic Review and Exploratory Clustering Analysis Using a Socio-Ecological Framework

analysis.research_question_and_background: Men who have sex with men (MSM) experience a disproportionate burden of human papillomavirus (HPV)-related disease, yet vaccination uptake remains uneven. This review synthesized evidence on uptake, willingness, multilevel barriers and opportunities, and vaccine-oriented outcomes among MSM and related sexual and gender minority populations.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This systematic review included 53 studies involving 169,241 participants, with 87.2% being MSM and 79% of studies being cross-sectional. The review focused on MSM and related sexual and gender minority populations when MSM-relevant findings could be extracted.
analysis.methods: Six databases were searched for original English- or Chinese-language studies published from 1 January 2010 to 31 December 2025. Barriers and opportunities were mapped using a five-level socio-ecological model, and study-level willingness–uptake patterns were explored using K-means clustering among nine studies reporting both outcomes.
analysis.main_results: Fifty-three studies involving 169,241 participants were included; 87.2% of participants were MSM, and 79% of studies were cross-sectional. Recurrent paired mechanisms involved knowledge and trust, provider recommendation and communication, service accessibility, community support, and eligibility and affordability.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Among MSM and related sexual and gender minority populations, HPV vaccination is shaped by interacting individual and structural conditions, with MSM remaining the principal focus of the evidence base. Nine studies contributed data to the exploratory clustering analysis; seven fell into low-uptake clusters, including three with high willingness but low uptake, which may indicate a possible study-level implementation gap.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Improving uptake is likely to require complementary strategies: universal, gender-neutral routine vaccination in adolescence before their sexual debut, and targeted catch-up for MSM who missed routine vaccination, supported by trusted provider endorsement, convenient service delivery, community engagement, and inclusive, affordable policy.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The thematic counts were study-level and unweighted, and the nine-study clustering analysis was exploratory rather than definitive. The evidence strength is moderate due to the systematic review approach but limited by the exploratory nature of the clustering and unweighted thematic counts.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review synthesized evidence on HPV vaccination uptake, willingness, barriers, and opportunities among MSM and related sexual and gender minority populations. Fifty-three studies involving 169,241 participants were included, with 87.2% being MSM. Barriers and opportunities were mapped across individual, provider, organizational, community, and policy levels. Recurrent mechanisms included knowledge gaps, provider communication, service accessibility, community support, and eligibility issues. Exploratory clustering identified seven low-uptake clusters, including three with high willingness but low uptake, suggesting implementation gaps. The review recommends universal gender-neutral vaccination in adolescence and targeted catch-up for MSM, supported by provider endorsement, accessible services, community engagement, and inclusive policies. Evidence strength is moderate but limited by unweighted thematic counts and exploratory clustering.

title: Allele-specific chromatin modifications of HPV-associated extrachromosomal DNAs in cervical cancer

analysis.research_question_and_background: Cervical cancer, a human papillomavirus (HPV) driven malignancy, is the fourth deadliest cancer in females. The study aimed to explore epigenetic differences between human-only and HPV-human hybrid extrachromosomal DNAs (ecDNAs) in cervical cancer.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study analyzed cervical cancer specimens to investigate ecDNAs, reporting that 30% of cervical cancers contained at least one ecDNA. It focused on HPV-human hybrid ecDNAs and human-only ecDNAs, examining their regulatory features.
analysis.methods: The researchers used long-read whole-genome sequencing (WGS) phasing data to separate chromatin immunoprecipitation sequencing (ChIP-seq) data into alleles, enabling the identification of allele-specific peaks in enhancers and promoters on ecDNAs.
analysis.main_results: HPV-human hybrid ecDNAs contained more active enhancers and promoters than human-only ecDNAs and invariably included the HPV oncogenes E6 and E7. Additionally, these ecDNAs showed allelic hypomethylation regions and enrichments for recombination hotspot motifs.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that epigenetic differences between ecDNA types may influence their regulatory functions, offering new insights into how HPV integration affects cervical cancer biology.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study highlights the role of epigenome disruption in cervical cancer and provides a framework for understanding how structural variations around HPV integration sites may alter regulatory architecture, potentially informing future diagnostic or therapeutic strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on abstract-only evidence, which limits the depth of analysis. However, the use of long-read WGS phasing data provides a robust method for examining ecDNA regulation, supporting a moderate confidence assessment.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the epigenetic differences between human-only and HPV-human hybrid extrachromosomal DNAs (ecDNAs) in cervical cancer. It reports that 30% of cervical cancers contain ecDNAs, with HPV-human hybrid ecDNAs showing more active regulatory elements and containing the oncogenes E6 and E7. The research reveals allele-specific chromatin modifications, suggesting that structural variations around HPV integration sites may influence regulatory architecture. These findings contribute to understanding the role of epigenome disruption in cervical cancer, potentially guiding future diagnostic or therapeutic approaches. However, the study is based on abstract-only evidence, which limits the depth of analysis, resulting in a moderate confidence assessment.

title: HPV Vaccination Knowledge, Perceptions and Beliefs Among School Health and Nutrition Supervisors in Bahawalpur District, Pakistan: A Cross- Sectional Study

analysis.research_question_and_background: Cervical cancer, predominantly caused by Human Papillomavirus (HPV), remains the fourth most common cancer in women globally, with over 90% of deaths occurring in low- and middle-income countries. School Health and Nutrition Supervisors' knowledge and training adequacy for HPV vaccination advocacy is largely unexamined.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This cross-sectional census survey assessed HPV vaccination knowledge, perceptions and beliefs among all 58 actively deployed School Health and Nutrition Supervisors across 21 Union Councils of Bahawalpur District, South Punjab, Pakistan, from September 2025 to April 2026.
analysis.methods: A validated structured self-administered questionnaire was used to collect data from all 58 supervisors, with analysis of predictors of knowledge including education, gender, school type and geographic location.
analysis.main_results: Respondents were predominantly male (69.0%), above 40 years of age (79.3%) and held postgraduate qualifications (98.3%). While 96.6% correctly identified the vaccination target age group and 82.8% recognised pre-debut vaccine efficacy, 55.2% incorrectly believed HPV vaccination provides 100% protection against cervical cancer. Only 37.9% knew the correct two-dose schedule and 41.4% recognised the continuing necessity of post-vaccination cervical cancer screening.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings demonstrate that a motivated, well-educated workforce is being systematically under-informed by inadequate training content, with direct implications for the quality and clinical accuracy of vaccine promotion delivered to parents and students.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Urgent reform of HPV training content, school-level communication protocols and locally adapted Urdu-language materials is required to improve vaccine promotion accuracy and effectiveness.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was limited to a single district in Pakistan and relied on self-reported data, though the census approach of including all 58 supervisors provides high representativeness for the target population.

analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study assessed HPV vaccination knowledge among 58 School Health and Nutrition Supervisors in Bahawalpur District, Pakistan. Despite high educational attainment (98.3% postgraduate), significant knowledge gaps were identified: 55.2% incorrectly believed HPV vaccination provides 100% protection against cervical cancer, only 37.9% knew the correct two-dose schedule, and 41.4% recognised the need for post-vaccination screening. All supervisors had recommended vaccination in the previous year, highlighting the critical role of accurate training in vaccine promotion. The study found education, gender, school type and location as significant knowledge predictors, emphasizing the need for urgent reform of training content and locally adapted materials to improve HPV vaccination advocacy quality.
